logline: A Madrid seamstress abandoned in Morocco with no money reinvents herself as a couturier to Nazi officers' wives - and a spy for the Allies - across the years of World War II.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.2/10 from audience ratings; the premiere drew 5.018 million viewers, the most-watched Antena 3 premiere in 12 years. IndieWire called it the cure for Downton Abbey withdrawal. Won Best Fiction at the Iris Awards.

pull_quotes.text: Spanish drama that will cure your hankering for Downton Abbey - gorgeous period costumes and a rebellious woman at its centre.

seasons.review_body: Adapted from Maria Duenas' 2009 bestselling novel by directors Inaki Mercero, Inaki Penafiel, and Norberto Lopez Amado, El tiempo entre costuras (The Time in Between) was a genuine cultural event in Spain on Antena 3. Its October 2013 premiere drew 5.018 million viewers - the most-watched Antena 3 premiere in twelve years. Adriana Ugarte plays Sira Quiroga, a Madrid dressmaker who follows her lover to Morocco, is abandoned and stripped of everything, then claws her way back through dressmaking for the wives of Nazi officers while passing intelligence to the Allies. The 11-episode run is deliberately operatic in its romantic register, which IndieWire compared favorably to Downton Abbey's gravitational pull on its audience. The IMDb audience score of 8.2 reflects the show's sustained popularity outside Spain, particularly in Latin America. The series won Best Fiction at Spain's Iris Awards.
